title: Using `Paste As Replacement` with `CSG` incorrectly pastes content
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in 4.7.stable ### System information Godot v4.7.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 4 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1062) - AMD Ryzen 7 9700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.16 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description Copying a piece of `CSG` and using `Paste As Replacement` onto a similarly named and structured node doesn't add all the new pieces of CSG, and causes the node names to become generated node names. The editor will still show the pasted CSG nodes, as if they exist, but on starting the project the CSG is no longer visible. Saving the scene and reopening will show that the new pieces aren't added to the scene. Notable is that **Undoing the action does not remove the visible CSG additions, nor renames the nodes back to their original name**. I have had similar issues in the past where the CSG does not remove the old CSG that it is replacing when using `Paste As Replacement`. This caused both to be permanently visible in-editor. I have had similar issues where the log spit out a lot of errors (I believe they were `could not add as child` errors). I suspect there are multiple issues, or multiple symptoms, when using `Paste As Replacement` with semi-complex CSG node structures. While I'm not certain, this could have something to do with: 1. The node names are the same. 2. The newly added CSG, which needs to be pasted and added, is a modified duplicate of a CSG that was already present in the paste location. 3. The paste location is a duplicate of the copy location. ### Steps to reproduce _A simplified scenario_ 1. Create a new Scene 2. Add a Node3D 3. Add a CSGBox as a child of the Node3D 4. Duplicate (Ctrl+D) the box and offset its position (2x) 5. Duplicate (Ctrl+D) the Node3D with the CSGBox children, and offset the box. 6. Duplicate (Ctrl+D) one of the boxes, modify it's extends. 7. Add new CSGCylinder nodes to the newly modified box. 8. Copy the entire Node3D with the new CSG nodes 9. Paste As replacement on the unadjusted Node3D 10. The names of the original nodes will show `@` in their name, due to them being generated. Only the three original CSG boxes are present, the newly added box and cylinders are not added, despite them being visible in the editor. 11. Undoing this action will not undo the action. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A. I might add one later, but it should be easily reproducible with the above steps.
